gloss: your kind consideration / kind patronage / generous attention (very formal honorific noun used in business letters and formal speech)

definitions.gloss: (in formal correspondence) your kind consideration; your gracious attention; the generous attention or patronage that the addressee bestows on the speaker or speaker's organization
definitions.explanation: A respectful noun used almost exclusively in formal business letters, ceremonial speeches, and the like. It refers to the kindness, attentiveness, or favor that the addressee shows toward the speaker. The {高|こう} prefix means "high" / "esteemed" and acts as an honorific raising the addressee's actions; {配|はい} carries the sense of "showing care" or "distributing attention." {高配|こうはい} appears in set greeting phrases at the opening of business letters and is rarely used in everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: {御高配|ごこうはい}{賜|たまわ}る。
examples.english: To receive your kind consideration. (very formal letter phrase)

examples.japanese: {平素|へいそ}より{格別|かくべつ}の{御高配|ごこうはい}を{賜|たまわ}り、{誠|まこと}にありがとうございます。
examples.english: We are sincerely grateful for the special consideration you regularly extend to us. (standard opening of a business letter)

examples.japanese: {今後|こんご}とも{変|か}わらぬ{御高配|ごこうはい}のほど、よろしくお{願|ねが}い{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: We humbly ask for your continued and unchanging support going forward.

examples.japanese: {皆様|みなさま}の{温|あたた}かい{御高配|ごこうはい}のおかげで、{無事|ぶじ}に{創立|そうりつ}{二十周年|にじゅっしゅうねん}を{迎|むか}えることができました。
examples.english: Thanks to all of your warm consideration and support, we have been able to safely mark our twentieth anniversary.

notes:
{高配|こうはい} is a very formal honorific noun referring to the addressee's kind consideration, generous attention, or patronage. It is almost always used with the honorific prefix {御|ご} as {御高配|ごこうはい} ({ご}{高配|こうはい}), and is typical of opening and closing greetings in Japanese business letters and formal speeches.

WHO/WHAT IT REFERS TO:
- The addressee's actions toward the speaker — never the speaker's own
- Implicit subject is always the recipient of the letter or audience of the speech

FIXED PHRASES (BUSINESS LETTER OPENINGS AND CLOSINGS):
- {平素|へいそ}より{格別|かくべつ}のご{高配|こうはい}を{賜|たまわ}り、{誠|まこと}にありがとうございます。 — Thank you sincerely for your special consideration extended to us as always.
- {日頃|ひごろ}より{格別|かくべつ}のご{高配|こうはい}にあずかり、{厚|あつ}く{御礼|おんれい}{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。 — We extend our deep thanks for the special consideration you regularly extend to us.
- {今後|こんご}とも{変|か}わらぬご{高配|こうはい}のほど、よろしくお{願|ねが}い{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。 — We respectfully request your continued, unchanged consideration going forward.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ご{高配|こうはい}を{賜|たまわ}る: to receive (your) kind consideration (very formal)
- ご{高配|こうはい}にあずかる: to be the recipient of (your) gracious attention
- ご{高配|こうはい}を{頂|いただ}く: to receive (your) kind consideration (slightly less archaic than {賜|たまわ}る)
- {格別|かくべつ}のご{高配|こうはい}: special / extraordinary consideration
- {温|あたた}かいご{高配|こうはい}: warm consideration
- {変|か}わらぬご{高配|こうはい}: unchanged / continuing consideration

SIMILAR FORMAL HONORIFIC NOUNS (BUSINESS-LETTER VOCABULARY):
- ご{愛顧|あいこ}: (your) patronage — very common in retail business letters
- ご{厚情|こうじょう}: (your) kindheartedness / deep goodwill
- ご{厚誼|こうぎ}: (your) deep friendship / cordial relations (between organizations or individuals)
- ご{支援|しえん}: (your) support — less archaic, broader use
- ご{協力|きょうりょく}: (your) cooperation — neutral formal, not specifically epistolary
- ご{愛顧|あいこ}を{賜|たまわ}る: to receive your patronage (parallel pattern)
- {引|ひ}き{立|た}て: backing / personal favor / patronage (often used in shop/business letters)

REGISTER AND USAGE NOTES:
- Extremely formal — appropriate for: business correspondence, formal speeches, ceremonial occasions, anniversary announcements, customer letters
- Inappropriate in: everyday conversation, casual writing, even most workplace internal email
- Always honorific in reference: never used about one's own behavior
- Modern business writing has begun to simplify this kind of language; younger writers may substitute ご{支援|しえん} or お{力添|ちからぞ}え for a less archaic feel
- Distinct in meaning from the homophone {後輩|こうはい} (junior colleague/student) and {荒廃|こうはい} (devastation) — pure context distinguishes them in writing, but voice intonation alone is identical
